import KitStatus from "../../../../components/ui/KitStatus.astro";

The drop-in is the [web components kit](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/elements/): one `pk-gate` around your app, in any framework. A recipe is that kit in one framework, with the property and event wiring that framework needs. To draw the screens yourself, take [your own UI](/docs/build/ui/#two-lanes) and the [headless models](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/elements/#headless); the Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact and Angular samples each include a small own-UI component over `viewOf()`.

<KitStatus kit="elements" />

Every recipe sets the gate's `input` as a **property**: it is an object, and an attribute can only carry a string. Each framework spells that differently, and each hears the gate's `pk-action` event its own way. Registering the elements is the import. The samples run on the Tidewater fixtures, with no Worker and no network.

```sh
pnpm add @polaris-key/elements
```

Until the package is published, the samples alias the repo's build. Run them from the repo root:

```sh
pnpm --filter @polaris-key/elements build
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --dir examples/ui/recipes
pnpm --dir examples/ui/recipes -r build
```

## htmx

<KitStatus kit="htmx" />

`pk-gate` sits outside the swapped region, so a swap never rebuilds it: it keeps its input and its place. htmx finds its `hx-*` attributes in the app as before.

```html
<pk-gate>
  <main>
    <section
      hx-get="./recent.html"
      hx-trigger="load"
      hx-swap="innerHTML"
    ></section>
  </main>
</pk-gate>
```

```html
<script type="module">
  import "htmx.org";
  import "@polaris-key/elements";
  document.querySelector("pk-gate").input = gateInput;
</script>
```

Set `input` in script, never as an attribute. Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/htmx/`.

## Vue

<KitStatus kit="vue" />

Tell the compiler the `pk-*` tags are not Vue components, bind `input` with `.prop` and listen with `@pk-action`.

```js
// vite.config.js
vue({
  template: {
    compilerOptions: { isCustomElement: (t) => t.startsWith("pk-") },
  },
});
```

```vue
<pk-gate :input.prop="input" @pk-action="onAction">
  <main><slot /></main>
</pk-gate>
```

Without `.prop`, Vue sets an attribute and the gate gets the string `[object Object]`. Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/vue/`.

## Svelte

<KitStatus kit="svelte" />

Svelte 5 sets a custom element's `input` as a property when it has one. Listen with `on:pk-action`. Leave Svelte's `customElement` compiler option off: that is for building elements, not using them.

```svelte
<pk-gate {input} on:pk-action={onAction}>
  <main><slot /></main>
</pk-gate>
```

Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/svelte/`.

## Solid

<KitStatus kit="solid" />

Solid sets attributes as strings unless told otherwise. `prop:input` assigns the property and `on:pk-action` listens for the element's own event.

```tsx
<pk-gate prop:input={gateInput(state())} on:pk-action={onAction}>
  <main>{props.children}</main>
</pk-gate>
```

Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/solid/`.

## Preact

<KitStatus kit="preact" />

Preact assigns a prop as a property when the element has one, so `input` takes the object as is. The event is `onpk-action`, lower case with the hyphen.

```tsx
<pk-gate input={gateInput(state)} onpk-action={onAction}>
  <main>{children}</main>
</pk-gate>
```

Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/preact/`.

## Angular

<KitStatus kit="angular" />

Angular 21. Add `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` so the template accepts `pk-*`, bind `[input]` (a property binding) and listen with `(pk-action)`. The event type is `CustomEvent`, so cast it in the template.

```ts
@Component({
  selector: "app-root",
  schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA],
  template: `
    <pk-gate [input]="input()" (pk-action)="onAction($any($event))">
      <ng-content />
    </pk-gate>
  `,
})
export class App {}
```

Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/angular/`.

## Tauri

<KitStatus kit="tauri" />

The front end is any recipe above in a Tauri v2 window: it builds and runs on its own. The reference shell in `examples/ui/recipes/tauri/src-tauri/` is committed and is not compiled in CI.

Grant the window one permission: opening `https` links in the system browser. The sign-in card and any store link need nothing more. No shell, file-system or http permission is needed.

```json
{
  "identifier": "default",
  "windows": ["main"],
  "permissions": [
    { "identifier": "opener:allow-open-url", "allow": [{ "url": "https://*" }] }
  ]
}
```

The Rust bridge is not shipped. Until it is, the elements run on fixtures, or live over `fetch` with a Worker. Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/tauri/`.

## Your design system

The gate takes a host design system through three seams. It writes no style into a shadow root.

1. **Tokens.** Map the host's shape tokens (radius, control height, focus width, font) onto `--pk-*` on `pk-provider`. The kit sets its own scales on `:host`, and a value that only inherits loses to that, so `pk-gate` and `pk-sign-in` take the provider's value explicitly with `inherit`.
2. **Structure.** `::part(primary)`, `::part(secondary)` and `::part(card)`.
3. **Accent.** Pass the host's brand color as `theme.accent`. The kit resolves it for contrast in each scheme, so colors stay with the scheme and the accent, not a token-by-token map.

```css
pk-provider {
  --pk-kit-radius-control: var(--hds-radius-control);
  --pk-kit-control-height: var(--hds-control-height);
}
pk-provider :is(pk-gate, pk-sign-in) {
  --pk-kit-radius-control: inherit;
  --pk-kit-control-height: inherit;
}
pk-gate::part(primary) {
  text-transform: uppercase;
}
```

```js
document.getElementById("provider").theme = {
  accent: "#b45309",
  product: { name: "Tidewater Studio", developer: "Harbor Audio" },
};
```

Keep the spacing scale and the three type weights. The theme value is on [Theming](/docs/build/ui/theming/). Sample: `examples/ui/recipes/byo-design-system/`.

## States to handle

The gate draws every state itself in each recipe. The states and panes are on the [web components page](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/elements/); in your own UI, `viewOf()` returns each state's copy keys.
